title: Cerebellar neural populations orchestrate dopamine reward signaling with single-trial precision
primary_outputs: Recompute individual-unit reward-outcome detection and contrast it with population-silencing timing/jitter on individual trials.
Recompute neural reward-outcome information across DCN/VTA units and evaluate sensitivity to temporal window and animal/session splits.

lineage_and_loader_evidence.input_level: Per-mouse spike/reward trial structures and DCN/VTA individual-trial tables.
lineage_and_loader_evidence.source_bridge: Separate data archive contains per-mouse NEVGroup.mat and ExpertFR.mat, and each mouse folder contains m01_SU_population_rw1/rw9.mat. Inspected A01_SingleUnitROC.m loads the same NEVGroup/ExpertFR files, then recomputes detection. a01_EphyReplot_acrossSU_SM_IPS.m iterates trial-wise SU_population arrays and derives population timing and IPStime. Set its data directory to each public mouse folder, replacing its example default. Matching DCN/VTA CSVs are documented as individual trials with reward label and spike-rate predictors. Full recording directories were enumerated; code-example data alone are not the basis of admission.
lineage_and_loader_evidence.limit: An empty missing-core-input list is not proof of schema compatibility, full-paper coverage or executable closure.
